question: Which of the following is an example of plasticity in plants?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Heterophylly**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Plasticity** in plants refers to the ability of plants to adapt their growth and development in response to environmental conditions or genetic factors.
 
• **Heterophylly** is a classic example of plasticity in plants. It refers to the occurrence of more than one type of leaf shape on the same plant.
 
• There are three types of heterophylly observed in plants:
 
 
• **Developmental heterophylly:** Different types of leaves arise at different stages of development in a plant. Example: Cotton.
 
• **Habitual heterophylly:** Different forms of leaves occur due to environmental conditions. Example: Buttercup.
 
• **Habitual heterophylly induced by genetic factors:** Leaf variations arise due to genetic makeup. Example: Coriander.
 
 
 
• Heterophylly allows plants to optimize their physiological and ecological functions, such as photosynthesis, water absorption, and reproduction, adapting them better to their environment. *Hence, the correct answer is Heterophylly.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Phototropism:**

 
 
• **Phototropism** is the growth movement of plants in response to light. It is not related to plasticity but is a directional growth mechanism. Example: Shoots grow towards light while roots grow away.
 
• This process involves the hormone **auxin**, which facilitates elongation of cells on the shaded side of the plant.
 
 
 
• **Vernalisation:**
 
 
• **Vernalisation** is the process of inducing flowering by exposing plants to prolonged cold temperatures. It is related to seasonal adaptation, not plasticity.
 
• For example, crops like wheat and barley require vernalisation for timely flowering.
 
 
 
• **Photoperiodism:**
 
 
• **Photoperiodism** refers to the response of plants to the duration of light and darkness in a day. It is responsible for regulating flowering and other physiological processes.
 
• Plants are categorized into **short-day plants**, **long-day plants**, and **day-neutral plants** based on their photoperiodic response.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Key Characteristics of Heterophylly:**

 
 
• It is a form of **adaptive plasticity** that allows plants to survive in varying environmental conditions.
 
• **Examples:** Cotton, coriander, and buttercup demonstrate different forms of heterophylly.
 
• Heterophylly plays a critical role in enhancing the efficiency of **photosynthesis** and **water use**, ensuring better survival and reproduction.
